# Three-load coherent scalar target-power acquisition

Research continuation, 28 October 2026. Mathematical construction and synthetic checks; no laboratory execution or historical novelty claim. This deliberately changes the acquisition interface. It does not contradict the original bounded-error lower bound for total returned intensity without an external reference.

## Source dependencies

Read directly: original `theory/first_harmonic_control.md`, `theory/finite_phase_harmonic.md`, `theory/harmonic_norm_calibration.md`, `alternatives/scope_stress.md`, `alternatives/multi_target_acquisition.md`, and `acquisition/rank_one_control_theory.md`. The new extraction proof below is self-contained. The conventional sequential control proof used below is the two-dimensional variational argument in the last source. This is not an independent whole-proof audit of the archive.

## 1. New physical interface

Keep the reciprocal passive source

\[
S=\begin{pmatrix}S_0&t\\t^T&s\end{pmatrix},\quad S^*S\preceq I,
\qquad T_z=S_0+\frac{z}{1-sz}tt^T.
\]

A calibrated reciprocal launcher sends `u`, `||u||<=1`, and its same source port receives

\[
h_z(u)=u^T T_z u=h_0(u)+\frac{z}{1-sz}a(u),
\quad a(u)=(t^T u)^2,
\quad p(u)=|a(u)|.
\]

The transpose is essential. A generic receiver projection does not have this identity. A reciprocal matched multiport launcher with unused source ports terminated provides an ideal realization. Mismatch, residual reflection, insertion loss and unequal transmit/receive transfer must be calibrated or enclosed. A reference is added downstream and isolated from the specimen; reference leakage changes the model unless bounded.

Only the target states `0,+r,-r`, `0<r<1`, are needed. In an ideal real reference impedance these are resistances `Z0`, `Z0(1+r)/(1-r)`, `Z0(1-r)/(1+r)`, hence `Z0,3Z0,Z0/3` for `r=1/2`. Switch and line parasitics must be calibrated at the target reference plane; state labels are not calibration.

## 2. Four real readings acquire each complex return

A passive 50:50 combiner with reference amplitude `R>0` gives one detector power

\[

\quad\theta\in\{0,\pi/2,\pi,3\pi/2\}.
\]

\[

+i(\widehat I_{\pi/2}-\widehat I_{3\pi/2})}{2R}.

28 October 2026. A continuation proof, not an inherited whole-proof audit.

## Contract and acquisition

Use the new calibrated coherent-reference oracle proved in

simultaneous deterministic error <=delta from p(u)=u*Gu. Include all readout,
load, reference, combiner, preparation, arithmetic and source-stability errors.
At fixed calibrated reference strength and radius, the new delta is proportional
to raw-intensity error. This assertion is not made for the original interface.

Acquire n diagonals d_hat_j. Let D=max_j d_hat_j and choose maximizing k.
If D<=4delta, return G_hat=0. Otherwise query, for j!=k,

    v_j=(e_j+e_k)/sqrt(2), w_j=(e_j+i e_k)/sqrt(2).

For the column q=G e_k, infer

    q_hat_j=p_hat(v_j)-(d_hat_j+D)/2
             +i[(d_hat_j+D)/2-p_hat(w_j)],
    q_hat_k=D,
    G_hat=q_hat q_hat*/D.

The sign convention is q_j=G_jk. Expand both quadratic forms to check it.
The full branch uses 3n-2 scalar queries, hence 36n-24 raw powers with the
twelve-reading receiver, plus twelve if a final verification is desired.
No nonzero pivot or informative pilot is supplied in advance.

tau above. Adding and subtracting q q*/D yields the data-dependent certificate

Thus, uniformly including G=0,

# Weak-target metrology with shared calibration and finite load tolerance

28 October 2026. A mathematical/executable extension; no hardware calibration
was performed.

## 1. Obstruction removed

Independently charging reference error against each bright return can overwhelm
a weak target. But the task uses differences: a shared background offset
cancels, a shared complex gain scales the residue, and fixed quadrature
imbalance also acts on differences. Retaining these correlations replaces a
background-sized absolute calibration floor by a relative floor. Arbitrary
drift does not have this property.

## 2. Acquired contract

For one command, h_z=h0+a z/(1-sz), |s|<=1, p=|a|<=1. Nominal loads are
z_l=0,+r,-r, 0<r<1. Actual loads satisfy |zeta_l-z_l|<=d_z and
|zeta_l|,|z_l|<=rmax<1. Reconstructed fields obey

    x_l=alpha h_zeta_l+beta conjugate(h_zeta_l)+b+e_l,
    0<gL<=|alpha|<=gU, |beta|<=bmax, |e_l|<=epsilon.

Alpha,beta,b are common across all three states. Their values may be unknown.
Local calibration provides these bounds and a warranted stability allowance;
epsilon includes readout, arithmetic and all unshared drift. No bound on the
common offset b is needed. Incident-power normalization and reciprocity remain
physical requirements; a finite fit does not prove an unrestricted stability law.

The receiver model follows from four fixed reference phasors L0,...,L3. With
physical I_k=|h+Lk|^2/2, nominal R>0, x=[I0-I2+i(I1-I3)]/(2R), and
X=L0-L2, Y=L1-L3, direct expansion gives

    alpha=(conjugate(X)+i conjugate(Y))/(4R),
    beta=(X+iY)/(4R),
    b=(|L0|^2-|L2|^2+i(|L1|^2-|L3|^2))/(4R).

Ideal quadrature has alpha=1,beta=b=0. Common detector gain multiplies these
coefficients. Static phase/amplitude imbalance need not be inferred as
independent errors on each load. Load-dependent coefficients belong in e_l.

## 3. Proof of the relative interval

For nominal fields define c=(h_r-h_-r)/(2r), d=(h_r+h_-r-2h0)/(2r).
Then c=a/(1-r^2s^2), d=rs c, so
